content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

We're at the start of a fresh first cycle — no prior artifacts exist, so I'll begin from Phase 1, Step 1 (Goal exploration). My job here is to understand *why* you want this before anything about screens or features.

---

Thanks — a bookmark app sounds like a great thing to build. Before we get into how it looks or works, I'd like to understand the purpose behind it, because that shapes everything else.

A few questions to get us aligned:

1. **When this is finished, what should be different from how things are for you now?** In other words, what problem with saving or managing bookmarks are you hoping this solves?

2. **Who is it mainly for** — just you personally, or would other people use it too?

3. Right now, when you come across something you want to save, **how do you handle it, and what's frustrating about that?**

4. When you say "manage," what does that bring to mind — for example, finding things again later, organizing them into groups, or something else? I want to check whether "saving bookmarks" is the real core, or whether the actual goal is something like *always being able to find what you saved*.

You don't need to answer all of these formally — just tell me in your own words what you're picturing, and I'll reflect back what I understand before we go further.

It’s mainly for me. Right now my bookmarks are scattered and become a pile I rarely revisit, because I can’t easily remember or find what I saved.

I want one place where I can save a link, have the useful page details filled in for me, add my own tags or notes, and later find it quickly through browsing or search. I’d also like to separate things I intend to read later from things I’ve finished, and put older bookmarks away without deleting them. The main goal is to make saved links genuinely easy to find and use again.

content:
That's really clear — thank you. Let me reflect back what I understand, to make sure I've got the direction right before we go further.

**What I understand your goal to be:**

> Today your bookmarks are scattered across places and pile up as something you rarely revisit, because you can't easily remember or find what you saved. You want **one place** where you can:
> - save a link and have the useful page details filled in for you automatically,
> - add your own tags or notes,
> - later find things quickly by browsing or searching,
> - separate things you *intend to read later* from things you've *finished*,
> - and put older bookmarks away (archive them) without deleting them.
>
> The real goal underneath all of this: **making saved links genuinely easy to find and use again** — not just saving them.

So I'm reading "saving" as the *means*, and "easy to find and reuse what you saved" as the *actual goal*. Saving is table-stakes; the value is in retrieval and staying on top of the pile.

**Two things to confirm:**

1. **Is that direction right?** Anything overstated, understated, or missing?

2. **What kind of app do you have in mind** — for example a web app you open in a browser, a mobile app, a desktop app, or a command-line tool? This just determines how I'll show you working screens as we go; it's not a commitment to any technology.
Yes, that direction is right. I’m picturing a personal web app that I can open in a browser. The emphasis on finding and revisiting things—not merely collecting more links—is exactly what I want.

That completes the rough edges across every part of the app — saving, tagging/notes, finding, reading status, archiving, editing, and deleting all now have their "what if" cases settled and recorded.

---

## Where we've landed

Here's the whole scope we've settled together, in plain terms:

1. **Save a link** — paste an address and the page's details (title, site, description) are filled in for you; it's kept even if those details can't be read, a bad address is refused, and saving the same link twice just points you to the one you already have.
2. **Tag and note** — add your own tags (choosing ones you've used before or creating new) and a free-form note.
3. **Find again** — search across the title, address, description, tags, and notes, and/or browse by clicking a tag; the two combine.
4. **To-read vs finished** — one-click marking, with focused tabs (All / To read / Finished); new links start as *To read*.
5. **Archive without deleting** — set older links aside into a separate Archived area, keeping everything, and restore them anytime.
6. **Edit anything** — fix the title, address (re-checked), description, tags, or note on any saved bookmark.
7. **Delete for good** — a clearly separate, confirmed permanent delete that won't be mistaken for archiving.
8. **A welcoming empty start**, and tidy handling of very long text.

Your bookmarks will persist between sessions (it's your personal, private collection).

---

Everything here has been built only as throwaway prototypes for exploring behaviour — **no real application has been built yet.**

**May I now switch from exploring to actually building this app for real, using exactly the scope above?** Once you approve, I'll move into development (Phase 2). If anything above looks off, tell me now and we'll adjust before I start.
